subject: Production private-connectivity: sticky VIP hairpin and asymmetric return path
messages:
From: Alex Geller <alex.geller@clearpath.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: SLA Ops <sla@clearpath.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent failures after maintenance – VIP hairpin + asymmetric returns

Hi Grace,

We pushed a small NAT/firewall rule change in our Clearpath VPC maintenance window at 02:00 UTC and immediately saw two issues:

- Internal clients calling the service VIP (10.20.10.5) intermittently get no response (hairpin fails) for TCP flows to port 443.
- External-origin requests succeed but a subset of responses appear to follow a different egress path and are being dropped by an upstream provider — causing 502s and session resets.

Attached are a short tcpdump (tcpdump_initial_20270809.pcap) and a traceroute we ran from an internal app instance (trace_pre_change.txt). We suspect sticky NAT or a sticky SNAT mapping that didn’t clear during the config change, but wanted your guidance before we start clearing conntrack across hosts.

Can Redwood confirm if anything on your side changed at that time or if you’ve seen similar hairpin / asymmetric return path issues in private deployments after maintenance? We’re out of hours on our side but can be available for a scheduled window.

Thanks,
Alex
Lead SRE, Clearpath Logistics

Hi Alex — thanks for the quick heads up and the captures. We haven’t pushed any config for your tenant during that window from Redwood.

Initial ask: can you share the output of "sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.20.10.5" from one app host and the iptables/nft rules for the edge NAT box? That will help us identify sticky mappings.

Plan (tentative):
- We’ll triage live traces with you during a brief coordination window.
- If conntrack state looks stale we’ll propose clearing specific entries on the edge NAT (not a full host-wide flush) and temporarily reduce the sticky timeout on the SNAT pool.
- Karthik and Marissa will lead the changes; I’ll coordinate with your ops to schedule a 5–10 minute test window.

I’ve opened NETOPS-4321 and linked a short playbook for VIP hairpin scenarios: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-playbook-vip-hairpin.

Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: 2027-08-09T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures after maintenance – VIP hairpin + asymmetric returns

Thanks Alex — quick notes from a network perspective: I’ve seen this pattern before where a combination of (a) sticky SNAT entries on the edge NAT/load-balancer, (b) a stale DNAT rule on an upstream firewall, and (c) rp_filter or asymmetric-route rejection on app hosts produces exactly these symptoms.

What I would check now:
- On the edge NAT: "conntrack -L | grep <VIP>" and look for old entries with long remaining time. If present, collect the tuple (src,dst,srcport,dstport,timeout).
- Confirm that the edge device isn’t doing per-flow sticky forwarding that pins return traffic to a different next hop after your maintenance change.
- On app hosts: check sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter and per-interface rp_filter. If rp_filter=1 and return path is asymmetric, kernel will drop packets.

If you can, please attach a short conntrack extract and iptables-save from the edge NAT. I can draft the exact commands to run so we avoid clearing unrelated sessions.

Cmds I’ll run if we schedule a window:
1) conntrack -L | grep 10.20.10.5 > /tmp/conntrack_vip.txt
2) iptables-save > /tmp/iptables_pre.txt
3) (If stale entries found) conntrack -D --orig-src <ip> --orig-dst 10.20.10.5 --orig-port-dst <port>

Marissa, can you prepare a minimal rollback plan for clearing the sticky entries?

- Karthik (oncall networking)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, Alex Geller <alex.geller@clearpath.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures after maintenance – VIP hairpin + asymmetric returns

Adding what I’ll execute during the test window. I’ll coordinate timing with Alex. Plan is conservative — no full conntrack clears.

Planned steps:
- Snapshot conntrack and iptables (saved to /tmp and uploaded to ticket).
- Clear specific conntrack tuples that reference the VIP and show long TTL.
- Reduce SNAT sticky timeout from 3600s -> 60s on the SNAT pool (edge LB) for 10 minutes.
- If hairpin still fails for internal clients, enable hairpin-mode on the LB (so internal->VIP is DNATed and DNATed back correctly).
- Observe for 30 minutes, then restore sticky timeout.

Attachments: planned_commands_20270809.sh (contains the exact commands and checks). I’ll run the change during the coordinated window and paste outputs to the ticket.

-Marissa
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Geller <alex.geller@clearpath.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-10T02:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures after maintenance – VIP hairpin + asymmetric return path

Thanks — we ran the planned window at 01:50 UTC. Marissa, your targeted conntrack deletions and the sticky timeout reduction improved the TCP hairpin behavior for most flows, but we still see intermittent 502s on some external requests.

I attached a second tcpdump (tcpdump_post_20270811.pcap) taken during the brief window and a short excerpt from our application logs showing fast retransmits and MSS negotiation differences. The interesting bit: some flows show fragmented packets and MSS clamping at an intermediate NAT (we see MTU 1460 vs 1500 negotiation). UDP flows to the VIP still struggle to hairpin — appears to be path MTU or filtering on fragments.

Can Redwood confirm whether your edge devices perform any MTU rewriting or have DF-clear behavior that could cause mid-path fragmentation?

Alex

Attachments: tcpdump_post_20270811.pcap (pcap)

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@clearpath.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-11T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures after maintenance – VIP hairpin + asymmetric return path

Alex — short status and root cause summary from Redwood’s side after the follow-ups:

What we found and fixed:
- Root cause: a combination of long-lived sticky SNAT entries on your edge NAT and an upstream route/next-hop change introduced during the maintenance window produced asymmetric return paths. Some return packets hit an upstream provider that performed PMTU behave differently (DF handling) causing fragmented packets to be dropped.
- Fixes applied: reduced SNAT sticky timeout on the edge pool temporarily, cleared targeted conntrack tuples, and added a route-policy on the edge to pin return traffic for the VIP to the same egress next-hop (ensures symmetric routing).
- For hairpin: we enabled hairpin-mode on the LB to handle internal->VIP DNAT correctly for TCP and UDP. That fixed most internal TCP flows; UDP required a small MTU clamp (set MSS=1420) for the few legacy endpoints that cannot handle fragmentation.

Post-change validation: we observed normal request rates for 24h and no new 502 spikes after we applied the egress pinning and MSS clamp. Attached are the post-fix captures and the commands we executed (planned_commands_20270809.sh).

Action items / follow-up:
- We updated the VIP hairpin playbook with a note about checking upstream provider MTU/DF behavior before doing wide conntrack clears.
- Please run a small canary for your UDP services during your next maintenance and report any regression.
- If you want, we can run a 30-minute joint dry-run to rehearse the steps.

Closing NETOPS-4321 — reopen if you see any recurrence. Thanks for the quick coordination.

Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
